prompt: A one-slot reservoir replaces its sample with every later stream item on a fair coin flip. Why is this biased?

options.text: It gives the first item too many chances to enter again.
options.explanation: The first item enters only once.

options.text: A reservoir must know the full stream length before starting.
options.explanation: Algorithm R works without knowing that length.

options.text: Later items get too much admission probability while earlier items face many replacement attempts.
options.explanation: Correct. Admission must shrink as the number of seen items grows.

options.text: Choosing each item with equal chance requires storing every item.
options.explanation: A correctly updated reservoir uses only its fixed sample storage.

workedExample: A late item gets a large chance to enter and has little time left to be replaced. An early item must survive many coin flips. Algorithm R balances these effects by drawing uniformly over all positions seen and admitting the newcomer only when its draw selects a sample slot.

prompt: In correct reservoir sampling, an early item enters more easily than a late item. Why can both still have the same final inclusion chance?

options.text: Earlier items are never removed after admission.
options.explanation: Later draws can replace any occupied sample slot.

options.text: Earlier items must survive more later replacement opportunities.
options.explanation: Correct. Easier entry is balanced by more opportunities to leave.

options.text: The algorithm sorts the reservoir by arrival time.
options.explanation: Sorting is not what establishes uniformity.

options.text: Every later item is guaranteed admission.
options.explanation: Only draws selecting a reservoir slot admit a later item.

workedExample: Final membership requires both admission and survival. A later item is harder to admit but has fewer later draws to survive. Algorithm R balances these probabilities across stream positions. Equal individual inclusion chances alone are weaker than uniform subsets; the uniform replacement rule supports the stronger subset property too.
